notes: BATCH AG (topical steroid / anti-infective creams). Routes are 'topical' so the engine treats them as local products. Topical products were NOT added to the systemic 'corticosteroid' group; a new group 'topical-corticosteroid' was created instead (no rules reference it yet; useful for duplication/potency checks). New group 'imidazole-antifungal' (miconazole, miconazole-hydrocortisone, mometasone-miconazole, clotrimazole; clotrimazole membership quoted from the Canesten pessary SmPC emc-2205) is used only as an allergen in the miconazole/hydrocortisone allergy rule. Topical miconazole was NOT added to azole-antifungal or cyp inhibitor groups, to avoid firing systemic azole interaction rules. NO UK PRODUCT: mometasone/miconazole (no UK combination on emc or MHRA Products) and isoconazole/diflucortolone (no UK product containing isoconazole; only single-ingredient diflucortolone SPCs from 2020 on MHRA Products, not used). Both have no rules and show only class-wide MHRA/BUMPS/SPS advice. SUBSTITUTE / PACK NOTES: (1) Hydrocortisone 1% cream has two UK SmPCs with different licences, kept as separate formulations: prescription-only (emc-12908: dose 2-3 times daily, children allowed, 4.3 = infected lesions) and pharmacy-sale hydrocortisone acetate (emc-102471: max 7 days, not under 10 without medical advice, 4.3 adds face/eyes incl. rosacea and perioral dermatitis, ano-genital area, broken skin, acne, occlusion, large areas). (2) Fusidic acid: clinic product is the cream; only the cream SmPC (emc-5510) is used (the ointment emc-5513 was read but not needed). (3) The clinic's fusidic acid/betamethasone product is sold under a non-UK brand name; the UK product with the same composition (fusidic acid 2% / betamethasone 0.1% as valerate cream, emc-983) is used. (4) Miconazole/hydrocortisone: the only current UK SmPC (emc-1557; MHRA Products has only this PL 15513/0303) is a pharmacy-sale pack. Its section 4.3 lists children under 10, ano-genital region, ringworm and secondarily infected conditions as excluded 'unless prescribed by a doctor'. Following the brief (4.3 = contraindicated), the under-10 age rule is level 'contraindicated' with the action saying 'unless prescribed by a doctor'; the integrator may prefer a lower level for prescriber users. CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES: pregnancy - pharmacy-sale hydrocortisone SmPC 'should not be used in pregnancy without medical advice', fusidic acid/betamethasone SmPC 'should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary', miconazole/hydrocortisone SmPC 'preferable to avoid' vs BUMPS 'Topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy' (betamethasone is not named in the BUMPS list; class statement used). Breastfeeding - pharmacy-sale hydrocortisone SmPC 'should not be used whilst breast-feeding unless recommended by a health care professional' and miconazole/hydrocortisone 'caution' vs SPS 'can be used'. All kept in the same rule's action text with both sources. AGE BOUNDS: SmPCs say 'children'/'infants and children' without an age; child rules use maxYears 18 and say so in the consequence. The elderly advice (miconazole/hydrocortisone) has no age and was not made a rule. MHRA: topical steroid withdrawal DSUs (Sept 2021, May 2024) and topical miconazole-warfarin DSU (June 2016) used. NICE NG153 (impetigo) and NG190 (infected eczema) used for fusidic acid place in therapy and course length. NOT FOUND: no BUMPS leaflet for topical miconazole or fusidic acid (404); no SPS breastfeeding page for topical miconazole; no SPS monitoring pages; SPS fusidic acid PGD page has content only in a Word attachment (not used). BRAND PRESCRIBING: none stated by any UK source. SECOND CHECK 2026-10-17 (audit/AF-AG.md): mometasone-miconazole and isoconazole-diflucortolone removed from topical-corticosteroid and imidazole-antifungal (no-uk-product medicines leave groups); no-uk-product status reconfirmed on emc and the MHRA products index. Miconazole/hydrocortisone under-10 rule kept contraindicated (SmPC 4.3) with concern text saying unless prescribed by a doctor. Unsupported rule consequences (corticosteroid may worsen/mask infection) replaced by source-backed wording; missing supporting quotes added; fusidic acid pregnancy rule added.
